summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require the Commonwealth Auditor-General to inspect and audit specified Australian banks, including banks identified as domestically systemically important by the prudential regulator.

Audits would examine derivatives exposures, housing loan portfolios, default provisions, off-balance-sheet liabilities and internal risk models, with findings reported to the Treasurer and Parliament.
The audit framework would require banks to assist authorised officers, while expressly excluding authority to report on the affairs of an individual bank customer.
changes: Authorised audit officers would gain access to bank premises and records at reasonable times.
The Auditor-General could copy bank documents and require information from bank employees and officials.
The Treasurer would have to provide funding for additional audit staff, resources and facilities.
summary.affected: Covered banks, their employees, the Auditor-General and the Treasurer are affected.
